title: Effect of Subtraction
statement: Let $W\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m:\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1\}^W$ be a memory, and let $i,j,k,a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$. If the words stored at addresses $j$ and $k$ are the $W$-bit encodings of $a$ and $b$, respectively, then executing the subtraction instruction with destination $i$ changes the memory to the function obtained by updating address $i$ with the $W$-bit encoding of $a-b$.
